extracted.intended_audience: depositors/patent applicants, patent agents, and laboratory staff preparing microorganism deposits under the Budapest Treaty
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural, technical and administrative requirements that biological depositary authorities specify for making, converting, storing and furnishing microorganism deposits under the Budapest Treaty (includes country-specific technical specs, forms, notifications, biosafety exclusions, and fee schedules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of deposit date and accession number (DBVPG)
rubrics_metrics.description: If requested, the DBVPG will communicate by telephone the date of deposit and the accession number of the yeast culture, before the official receipt is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an unofficial/provisional communication only; the official receipt follows the formal acceptance/viability procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply of viability statement to patent agent (DBVPG)
rubrics_metrics.description: If requested, the DBVPG will send a copy of the viability statement to the patent agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DBVPG will provide viability documentation to a patent agent upon request; depositor should request if they want agent copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting a previous deposit to Budapest Treaty (DBVPG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits made outside the Budapest Treaty can be converted by the original depositor to deposits under the Budapest Treaty. In this case, the fees normally payable under the Budapest Treaty are due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements for conversion are the same as for an original deposit; depositor must follow original-deposit requirements and pay Treaty fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for making a new deposit (DBVPG)
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a new deposit, the depositor must fill in a deposit form which includes a declaration on the pathogenicity of the yeast culture, and the depositor must send a copy of the documents of the declaration indicated in Rule 6.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shipment must follow the technical requirements and procedures described in point 1(b) (i.e., the technical/form/quantity rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of samples: requester procedures and importer obligations (DBVPG)
rubrics_metrics.description: The DBVPG does not inform requesting parties about the procedure to be followed for the request, and does not provide the forms of request which can be obtained from the relevant Patent Office. The DBVPG assumes that the requesting parties have satisfied all the national requirements concerning importation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters must obtain and complete the appropriate Patent Office request forms and satisfy import rules themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to depositor on furnishing samples (DBVPG)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the DBVPG delivers samples of the deposited microorganism to third parties, it notifies the depositor by letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification is by letter; depositor will be informed when third-party supplies are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cataloguing of Budapest Treaty deposits (DBVPG)
rubrics_metrics.description: The DBVPG does not include the deposits made under the Budapest Treaty in its catalogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should not expect public catalog listing from DBVPG for Treaty deposits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of fees (DBVPG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees listed for storage and services: Storage for 30 years: EUR 650; Issuance of a viability statement: EUR 50; Furnishing of a sample - agar slants: EUR 40; - freeze-dried samples: EUR 15; Communication of information: EUR 25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees apply as listed; confirm current rates with DBVPG as these may change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of microorganisms accepted (IZSLER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepts animal bacteria isolated from tissues and organs and from food; human and animal viruses. IZSLER accepts microorganisms according to Directive 2000/54/EC; animal pathogens of risk level 1 and 2 will be accepted; those listed in article 265 and 265 bis of national law will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No mixed microbiological cultures will be accepted (unless sent separately). IZSLER reserves the right to refuse biological resources that represent a high hazard or that cannot be processed for technical reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage methods and temperatures (IZSLER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Biological resources can be sent frozen or freeze-dried and their storage will be made at -20°C and -80°C according to the method that allows a long-term preservation of vitality and maintenance of the characteristic of the material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor should select preservation method compatible with long-term viability and inform IZSLER of form sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, quantity and concentration requirements (IZSLER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bacteria and viruses should be sent frozen or freeze-dried cultures. Twelve vials must be provided from a single preparation and at a concentration of no less than 10^5 viable units / vial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material must be tested and free from contamination by the depositor prior to shipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability testing time estimates (IZSLER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time for viability testing: Bacteria average 14 days (up to 3 weeks); Human and Animal Viruses average 20 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slow-growing microorganisms require longer testing; depositors should allow for extended testing in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor checks and renewal of stocks (IZSLER)
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, IZSLER does not prepare batches of bacteria and viruses; when batches are exhausted it requests the depositor to make a new deposit. Only in particular cases and following previous written consent of the depositor, IZSLER can prepare a new batch. The depositor has to control the quality characteristics of the material. A portion of each original material supplied by the depositor is stored as master deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If IZSLER prepares batches, depositor remains responsible for checking authenticity/quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and contract requirements (IZSLER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Official language of IZSLER is Italian; communications are accepted in Italian and English. A contract between IZSLER and the depositor must be prepared and signed by both parties. The depositor acknowledges conditions of the Budapest Treaty, rules to be observed and relative liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract must include declarations of quantity/form/characteristics/biological risk/payment and compliance with Budapest Treaty and IZSLER rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Import and quarantine / transport requirements (IZSLER)
rubrics_metrics.description: IZSLER requests an import authorization from Italian Ministry of Health. No quarantine regulation must be followed for microorganisms that are accepted by IZSLER. Transport of infectious material in Italy is subjected to packaging conforming to international regulations on transport of hazardous materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor must obtain necessary permits and ensure packaging complies with international hazardous materials rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making the original deposit: forms and notifications (IZSLER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositors must complete and sign contract and deposit forms. A BP/7 form is required for later indication/amendment of scientific description or taxonomic designation. Official notifications: receipt and viability statement via international forms BP/4 and BP/9; attestation on BP/8 for changes; notification of furnishing to third parties on BP/14. Official forms sent only after viability testing and when deposit is accepted; accession number equals registration number. IZSLER will communicate date of deposit and number by e-mail before official statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send original deposit documents with the biological resource; advised to send documents by e-mail beforehand to expedite processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply of information to patent agent (IZSLER)
rubrics_metrics.description: IZSLER will provide, if requested, information to the patent agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor or agent should request copies if they want agent to receive notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting other deposit types to Budapest Treaty deposit (IZSLER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposit of other types (open deposit, safe deposit) can be converted by the depositor into deposit under the Budapest Treaty. Depositor must indicate original deposit date, accession number, depositor info, request conversion and maintain deposit/distribution during the period specified in rule 9.1. Either move batch to new deposit or prepare a new batch. New deposit is subject to Treaty rules and administrative requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversions are treated as new deposits and subject to all Treaty administrative rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of samples procedures and proof of entitlement (IZSLER)
rubrics_metrics.description: IZSLER notifies third parties of the correct procedures to order patent microorganisms and will send model request form BP/12. Third parties receive microorganism following provision of evidence that they are allowed to work with it. All documents including import permits are requested for overseas requests, or a declaration that no authorization is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor will be informed via BP/14 when samples are furnished to third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cataloguing policy (IZSLER)
rubrics_metrics.description: IZSLER does not publish list of deposits under the Budapest Treaty in any published catalogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should not expect public disclosure in IZSLER catalogues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of fees (IZSLER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed fees given for a range of services (examples): Storage -- Bacteria EUR 608.80, Animal viruses EUR 701.27, storage frozen liquid nitrogen EUR 1,448.27; Viability statements: base 60/100/150 EUR depending on type; Furnishing of a sample: bacteria EUR 105, virus EUR 400; Communication of information or issuance of an attestation EUR 50. VAT added per Italian regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees vary by service/type; check precise fee applicable to organism/form and confirm VAT treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance notes availability (IZSLER)
rubrics_metrics.description: IZSLER provides a written note for the request of deposit under the Budapest Treaty available on its home page; further information can be requested by e-mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should consult the online guidance note and contact IZSLER for clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of microorganisms accepted and exclusions (IPOD, Japan)
rubrics_metrics.description: IPOD accepts protozoa, plant cell cultures, seeds and algae, EXCEPT microorganisms classified as BSL 3 or 4 per NITE guidelines; microorganisms requiring containment measures P3 or P3P; and mixtures of undefined and/or unidentifiable microorganisms. IPOD reserves the right to refuse deposits that are technically or legally too difficult to manage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check national biosafety/classification rules before deposit; mixture and high-biosafety organisms are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and minimum quantities required (IPOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Microorganisms should be submitted as frozen samples or agar stab/slant cultures. Minimum replicates: plant cell cultures 5 slant cultures; protozoa and algae 10 tubes or 5 agar stabs or 5 slant cultures; seeds 100 packs / 25 seeds per 1 pack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the exact form and replicate numbers for each biological resource type to meet deposit acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability testing time estimates (IPOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average length of time required for testing viability is 20 days, but in some cases may take as long as 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should plan for long lead times in certain cases and not assume the provisional accession is final until tests and payments complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositary preparation of batches and stock renewal (IPOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: IPOD prepares its own batches of the microorganism at the time of deposit by subculturing material supplied by the depositor. New batches are prepared as necessary thereafter for renewal of diminishing stocks. For seeds and frozen samples, IPOD stores samples originally supplied by depositor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor should expect IPOD to prepare distributions from its own subcultures and may need to replenish supply if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative language, contract and depositor obligations (IPOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Official language is Japanese; power of attorney and other attached documents can be in another language but must be accompanied by a Japanese translation. IPOD does not enter into a written contract; by signing the deposit form, the depositor surrenders any right to withdraw the microorganism during the required storage period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure translations accompany non-Japanese documents. Understand signing deposit form binds depositor to non-withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original deposit forms and notifications (IPOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositors must complete the equivalent of model form BP/1. For later amendments use BP/7. Official notifications: receipt and viability statement on BP/4 and BP/9; attestation on BP/8; notification of release to third parties on BP/14. IPOD has its own standard forms for other notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional accession numbers may be given before official receipt, but become official only on completion of viability test and payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply of information to patent agent (IPOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: IPOD does not routinely ask for the name/address of a patent agent. IPOD will send copies of the receipt and viability statement either to the depositor or to his agent if requested, but not to both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose whether copies should go to depositor or agent; request explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of prior deposits to Budapest Treaty (IPOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits made outside the provisions of the Budapest Treaty may be converted by the original depositor to Budapest Treaty deposits only if they were originally made for patent purposes. Administrative requirements for conversion are similar to an original deposit, except the depositor must supply a copy of the receipt of the previous deposit. Conversions subject to normal storage fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure original deposit was made for patent purposes and supply previous receipt for conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making a new deposit (IPOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositor required to complete model form BP/2 when making a new deposit and to supply copies of relevant documents required by Rule 6.2. Receipt and viability statement are issued on international forms BP/5 and BP/9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow BP/2 and Rule 6.2 documentary requirements exactly to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of samples: requester forms and health/safety agreement (IPOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: IPOD will provide model request form BP/12 and/or forms used by individual industrial property offices. Requesting parties are required to complete IPOD form BP/14 (Acknowledgement and Agreement for Furnishing and Use of Samples) to comply with health and safety requirements. IPOD assumes requesting party has met import requirements of his country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters must complete BP/14 and provide evidence of entitlement and import permits where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cataloguing policy (IPOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPOD does not list Budapest Treaty deposits in its published catalog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should not expect public catalog listing from IPOD for Treaty deposits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and taxes (IPOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule of fees includes storage (original deposit JPY 175,000; new deposit JPY 33,000), issuance of attestation JPY 3,000, issuance of viability statements and furnishing fees (e.g., JPY 29,000, 3,000, 41,000, 3,000 as listed). Japanese consumption tax applies to certain items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm current fees and tax applicability; shipping/handling for overseas shipments charged separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of microorganisms accepted and exclusions (NPMD, Japan)
rubrics_metrics.description: NPMD accepts actinomycetes, animal cell cultures (including hybridomas and human cell cultures), archaea, bacteria, bacteriophages, embryos, fungi, plasmids (in hosts or not) and yeasts, EXCEPT microorganisms belonging to biosafety level 3 or 4 per NITE classification, those requiring containment measures level P3/P3A/P3P, and mixtures of undefined/unidentifiable microorganisms. NPMD may refuse deposits technically or legally too difficult to manage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify biosafety classification and containment requirements before attempting deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable forms and minimum quantities (NPMD)
rubrics_metrics.description: NPMD accepts lyophilized or frozen samples; where difficult, agar stabs/slants acceptable. Required quantities: for e.g., actinomycetes/archea/bacteria/bacteriophages/fungi/plasmids/yeasts: 10 ampoules, 10 tubes, 5 agar stabs or 5 slant cultures; animal cell cultures and embryos: 12 tubes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conform to the specific replicate numbers for each biological category to avoid rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability testing time estimates by organism type (NPMD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average viability testing times: plasmids 1 day; bacteria 3 days; yeasts 5 days; actinomycetes/fungi/bacteriophages 7 days; embryos 7 days; animal cell cultures (including hybridomas and human cell cultures) 3 to 4 weeks. In some cases testing may take longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow for extended processing for complex or slow-growing materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor checks, storage of original material, and stock renewal (NPMD)
rubrics_metrics.description: NPMD stores samples originally supplied by the depositor and does not subculture material supplied by depositor. Depositor is required to supply samples to replenish diminishing stocks. If requested, NPMD can make its own preparations by subculture at additional fee; in that case depositor must test for authenticity of NPMD-prepared samples and inform NPMD of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor liability includes replenishment and authentication if NPMD prepares batches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative language, contract and depositor obligations (NPMD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Official language is Japanese; requests may be in Japanese or English. NPMD enters into a written contract with the depositor which binds depositor to provide necessary information, replenish microorganism at his own expense if NPMD cannot furnish samples, and not to withdraw the deposit during the required storage period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a formal contract imposing obligations and potential replenishment duties on the depositor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making original deposit and notifications (NPMD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositors required to complete BP/1 equivalent plus NPMD form 2. Use BP/7 for later amendments. Official notifications: receipt and viability on BP/4 and BP/9; attestation on BP/8. NPMD will inform date of deposit and provisional accession number before official receipt, but it becomes official only on completion of viability test and payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide required forms promptly; provisional notices are not final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply of information to patent agent (NPMD)
rubrics_metrics.description: NPMD does not ask for patent agent details routinely, but if requested will supply the receipt and viability statement through the depositor’s patent agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit agent request explicitly if you want agent copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of samples: local request forms and samples origin (NPMD)
rubrics_metrics.description: NPMD advises third parties on correct procedures and supplies request forms used by Japan Patent Office. Requesting parties must complete NPMD form 14 (Acknowledgement and Agreement). When responding to overseas requests, NPMD assumes requestor met import requirements. All samples may be from preparations supplied by the depositor, except those not supplied as lyophilized or frozen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties must complete NPMD forms and satisfy import/health requirements; samples may come from depositor-supplied material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cataloguing policy (NPMD)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NPMD does not publish any catalogue of Budapest Treaty deposits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should not expect public catalog listing from NPMD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for depositors (NPMD)
rubrics_metrics.description: NPMD provides pamphlets for the guidance of prospective depositors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult NPMD pamphlets for country-specific practical instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds accepted and exclusions (MSCL, Latvia)
rubrics_metrics.description: MSCL accepts bacteria, fungi (including yeasts), plasmids in a host with the exception of pathogenic microorganisms of hazard group 3 or 4. Microorganisms having special requirements for cultivation which MSCL cannot carry out shall not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MSCL reserves refusal for host/technical incapabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and minimum replicates (MSCL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultures must be in the form of agar stabs (slants) or lyophilized. Minimum replicates: five stabs (slants) or 25 lyophilized ampoules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide uncontaminated material in required numbers to meet acceptance criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability testing time estimates (MSCL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time required for viability testing is 7 days, but in some cases may take 20 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow for longer testing for certain organisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor checks, contamination handling and storage (MSCL)
rubrics_metrics.description: MSCL prepares its own batches by subculturing material supplied by the depositor and routinely asks the depositor to check authenticity of preparations made. MSCL routinely checks newly received deposits for contamination and, if contaminated, returns them to the depositor. MSCL stores original material supplied by the depositor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor should expect to authenticate MSCL-prepared batches and to re-submit if contamination occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative language and contract (MSCL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Official language is Latvian; communications accepted in English, German and Russian. MSCL does not enter into a written contract, but by signing deposit forms depositor surrenders right to withdraw during required storage period and accepts distribution according to relevant patent requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide documents in accepted languages; signing imposes non-withdrawal obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making original deposit forms and pre-notification (MSCL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositors must complete MSCL–BP/1 (equivalent to BP/1). For new deposits use BP/2 equivalent and BP/7 for later amendments. Official notifications use international forms; unofficially, if requested, MSCL will telephone/fax date and accession number before official receipt but only after a positive viability test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect provisional unofficial communications only after positive viability testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply to patent agent and conversion rules (MSCL)
rubrics_metrics.description: If requested, MSCL will send copies of receipt and viability statement to both depositor and patent agent. Deposits made outside Treaty may be converted only if originally for patent purposes; conversion subject to normal storage fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask MSCL to supply agent copies explicitly; provide prior receipt for conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of samples and cataloguing (MSCL)
rubrics_metrics.description: MSCL advises third parties on correct request procedures and will provide BP/12 and/or other request forms. All samples furnished by MSCL are from batches of its own preparations. Depositors notified on BP/14 when samples furnished. MSCL does not list Budapest Treaty deposits in its published catalog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties must use provided forms and accept MSCL-prepared distribution batches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of fees (MSCL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees: Storage EUR 426.86; Issuance of a viability statement EUR 42.69; Furnishing of a sample (plus expedition cost) EUR 42.69. Fees subject to VAT (21%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm VAT and shipping costs; fees apply as listed at time indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of microorganisms accepted; special conditions and exclusions (CBS, Netherlands)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBS accepts fungi, yeasts, bacteria, plasmids in pure form or in a host and phages that can be maintained with routine laboratory techniques without significant modification during appropriate storage. Strains requiring special cultural conditions can be accepted under special conditions and are subject to additional fees. Certain pathogenic bacteria are accepted only when they can be maintained by designated national institutes; Bacillus anthracis and Yersinia pestis are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact CBS about plant pathogens and conditional acceptances; additional fees may apply for special-handling organisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred forms and minimum replicates (CBS)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBS prefers lyophilized preparations. Minimum replicates: Fungi 12 lyophilized or 2 agar cultures; Yeasts 12 lyophilized plus 1 agar or 2 agar; Bacteria 12 lyophilized plus 1 agar or 3 agar; Plasmids (purified DNA) minimum quantity of 50 g (as listed); Phages 10 ml with a titre of at least 10^9 pfu/ml.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If depositor cannot provide lyophilized material, CBS can prepare lyophilized or frozen batches for a fee (examples: Euro 125 for 10 ampoules freeze-dried, Euro 175 for 10 frozen straws, Euro 500 for phage lysate prep). Depositor must check authenticity of CBS-prepared batch and inform CBS of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability testing times (CBS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average viability testing time: fungi, bacteria, plasmids in hosts or purified DNA and phages — 2 weeks; yeasts — 1 week. (Note: some cases may take longer, especially if unusual antibiotics/additives required.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should account for longer testing when specialized media or conditions are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor authentication and stock renewal (CBS)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBS routinely asks the depositor to check authenticity of a sample of batch prepared by CBS. New batches are prepared when necessary to renew stocks. CBS always keeps a portion of the original material supplied by the depositor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor responsibility includes checking authenticity of CBS-prepared material and informing CBS of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative language, contract and import/quarantine assistance (CBS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Official language is English; communications also accepted in Dutch, German and French. CBS does not enter into a written contract; by signing deposit forms depositor surrenders right to withdraw and accepts that the microorganism will be distributed according to patent requirements. CBS will advise depositors about import/quarantine regulations and make arrangements for transportation/licenses (fees on request).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact CBS in advance for precise instructions, especially for plant pathogens.
